working class developer. Well, this week
the joke's on them because PHP finally

when two bugs, now known as PHP 2 Shell,
let anyone with an internet connection
run whatever they want on any PHP server
released in the last decade by stringing
together two flaws in how PHP manages
memory. The first one comes from the
fact that every PHP server has a memory
limit and when a request goes over it,
it uses an old C trick to jump straight
to the end of the request without
finishing or cleaning up anything it was
working on. The second one comes from
the fact PHP recycles the same process
for every request and the last one left
in memory doesn't always get cleared
before the next one arrives. For 20
years, neither of those was a problem,
but recently researchers figured out that if you combine them by pushing PHP
over its memory limit at exactly the
right moment, like halfway through a
file upload, it'll leave behind half-baked data that the next request
can pick up and use, which if exploited
means anyone can run their own code on
your server. And this vulnerability was
actually found a few months ago by a
security firm using GPT 5.6 Soul, who

terms meant that anyone could start
impersonating any website on the internet by simply guessing a number

valid HTTPS certificate. eMudhra, the company responsible for the
